reviews.title: Almost perfect; breaks every other update
reviews.text: This would be the absolute best app ever, especially for a hyperpolyglot studying “key”/“gateway” languages into most languages they could want to learn. Developers have a major, major issue of not troubleshooting their updates well enough and every other update deletes a course for a while (my hebrew course is currently gone), completely disables the play-speed options (sometimes entirely, usually when screen mirroring on TV), or breaks the app entirely and just gives an error screen for 2 days. I want to preach about how amazing this app is when it works, except thats pretty nullified when it doesnt even work. Constantly.

reviews.title: Poor content quality and customer service
reviews.text:
I wanted to share my experience with Lingopie in case anyone is considering subscribing. I personally wouldn’t recommend it (TL):

The content library is much smaller than I expected. After subscribing, I found there wasn’t enough content that interested me, so I decided not to continue.

The customer support experience was disappointing. My annual subscription auto-renewed, but I don’t recall receiving any reminder before the renewal. I only discovered the charge after reviewing my bank statement about a week later and canceled the subscription immediately. I contacted support right away to request a refund, but they repeatedly refused and instead offered to downgrade me to a quarterly plan. What surprised me is that the quarterly plan costs about half of what I had just been charged for the annual renewal, which made the offer feel like an attempt to retain me as a paying customer rather than fairly resolve the issue. I also asked multiple times whether a renewal reminder had been sent before the charge, but they never directly answered that question and instead kept referring me back to their Terms of Service.

I understand that it’s ultimately my responsibility to cancel a subscription before it renews. My frustration is with the poor customer service, the lack of a direct answer about the renewal reminder, and the inflexible handling of the situation.

If you’re considering Lingopie, I’d recommend reviewing the content library carefully before subscribing and setting your own reminder well before the renewal date if you’re not sure you’ll keep the subscription.

reviews.text:
Hello,

I signed up because your app clearly advertised:

$83.99 annually after a 7-day free trial

However, after I entered my payment information, a $41 payment was attempted. Although the payment was declined, that isn’t consistent with what your advertisement stated. If today’s charge was supposed to be $0, why was a $41 charge attempted?

Please explain why this happened and clarify your billing practices, as the information shown before I signed up does not match my experience.

Thank you.

reviews.title: There is no way to contact app support and get things fixed except writing a review.
reviews.text:
I have three suggestions:

1. There’s no way to contact you. The only way to provide feedback is through an app review. There’s no email address or in-app feedback option.
2. The streak system is frustrating. If I practice multiple times a day, I should be able to maintain my streak. Instead, the streak section locks for 24 hours, forcing me to wait until the exact time it unlocks again. If I miss that window, I lose my streak even though I’m using the app regularly. I shouldn’t have to watch the clock just to keep a streak. Please let users access the streak section whenever they want.
3. Some translations are incorrect. I report them using the flag, but they never seem to be fixed. For example, I’ve tapped a French word and the English translation simply repeats the French word instead of giving the English meaning. Are the translation reports being reviewed?

reviews.title: The search is over
reviews.text:
So glad this app exists. I love reading in French, and Lingopie allows me to learn and study new words while watching videos, which has boosted my vocabulary in a short time. The combination of video, translation, games, and flashcards using spaced repetition has made this possible.

Often on other platforms, like Netflix, the dialogue doesn’t match the closed captions. That’s not the case with Lingopie, which I really appreciate.

I am watching The Daltons, a French animated comedy series. The episodes are short and packed with a ton of new and very specific vocabulary that would have taken a lot of reading elsewhere to find.

The reason I am giving four stars is that the translation of the script sometimes doesn’t make sense. You can report errors and provide a new translation, which is great. However, the content is also very limited. It would be wonderful if Lingopie could mimic Language Reactor and develop an extension that can be used while streaming on other platforms. Lingopie has a nice, easy-to-use interface, and it would be great to be able to use it elsewhere.

Thank you for the great service you provide!

reviews.title: AI subtitles with mistakes you’d expect
reviews.text:
The app is difficult to work. The AI subtitles are hideous. They use AI to get the subtitles native to the target language and then translate. 

It will mishear the original word and give you a completely inaccurate translation. It also doesn’t note or separate when the next speaker starts. Thats especially important when languages use different sentence structures. The vocab feature can be inaccurate having it attached grammar to random words and have you learned it as the word itself. The test features use AI so you may have the correct answer listed twice, but only one is correct. Which one? No one knows.
